The selected source forest operation explicitly constructs necessary influence events using probes outside all inserted sites, before bounding the signed kernel. Simultaneous static pivotality is a subset of that necessary-influence event. Thus k=1,2 event bounds, Mecke/lattice normalization and the diagonal term support the claimed second-moment mechanism. A signed mixed-derivative bound alone would not. Parent has not independently reread all localization/arm companions or the complete removal of the box cutoff this round.

The stationary single-site history law is P0+q_e w_e exactly. Refresh rate r_e means flip rate r_e/2, and averaging the two fair initial states gives the one-flip coefficient 1/4. A per-site Taylor remainder cannot be multiplied naively by all sites; the claimed limit instead needs the uniform centered-weight expansion and its multilinearity. The full sewing/calibration application remains within the incomplete independent-review scope.

For a finite crossing vector, two changes in a small overlapping interval have probability O(h^2), while changes near the time endpoints cost O(h). Summing O(T/h) intervals pays the finite-state common-clock J1 tightness criterion. Counting a simultaneous multi-quad change once is necessary.

The countable crossing-coordinate metric has deterministic tail at most 2^(-m). Truncating the coordinate vector changes the whole path by that uniform bound, so finite-vector tightness extends to its stated product-state path space. This does not identify it with the geometric quad-crossing topology or a spatial pivotal process.

Two independently colored/clocked replicas on common geometry identify the second moment of conditional expectations. Once the one- and two-replica path limits are established, compact tightness sets and finite Lipschitz nets yield quenched bounded-Lipschitz convergence. A finite net over the entire noncompact path space would not be valid.

For x<=1/(4K), the roots are uncapped. Both are between 1/x-K and 1/x+K, giving reciprocal-kernel Lipschitz constant at most 4x^2 and inverse derivative lower bound 4x^2/9. The resulting transform difference is at most 9 W1, including its limiting mean value at zero.

For larger x, evaluating at a=max(b_mu,e_nu)+t puts both supports at distance at least t. The coupling error is at most epsilon/t^2. If b_nu>a, then b_nu<=5K and the derivative magnitude is at least 1/(36K^2); otherwise the simpler edge-plus-t bound suffices. Symmetrization and t=(72K^2 epsilon)^(1/3) give coefficient below 7, with the zero-epsilon case handled separately.

The source variational comparison has exactly the factor 1/2 times the sup-norm transform difference. This transfers S149 to pressure without differentiating the limit or exchanging an infimum and supremum.
